subskill: One-variable equation, k on a binomial; count k
prompt:
k(x + 4) = 2x - 12
In the equation above, k is a constant. How many integers k with -6 ≤ k ≤ 11 make the equation have a solution less than 4?
explanation: Collect the x-terms: kx + 4k = 2x - 12, so (k - 2)x = -4k - 12. Treat k = 2 as its own case: the equation becomes 0 = -20, which is false, so there is no solution and k = 2 does not count. For k ≠ 2 the solution is x = (-4k - 12)/(k - 2), and we need x < 4. When k > 2, k - 2 is positive, so -4k - 12 < 4(k - 2), which gives k > -1/2; every k from 3 to 11 works (9 values). When k < 2, k - 2 is negative, so multiplying reverses the inequality: -4k - 12 > 4(k - 2), which gives k < -1/2; the values k = -6, -5, -4, -3, -2, -1 work (6 values). The total is 9 + 6 = 15. Choice 12 comes from multiplying by k - 2 without checking its sign: k > -1/2 for every k, which keeps k = 0, 1 and the no-solution value k = 2 but loses all six negative values. Choice 8 comes from a sign slip that writes the solution as (-4k - 12)/(2 - k); then every k below 2 appears to work and no k above 2 does. Choice 6 keeps only the branch where k - 2 is negative.
solve: let n=0; for(let k=-6;k<=11;k++){ const a=k-2, b=-12-4*k; if(a===0) continue; if(b/a<4) n++ } return n

distractor_solve.6: let n=0; for(let k=-6;k<=11;k++){ if(-12-4*k > 4*(k-2)) n++ } return n
distractor_solve.8: let n=0; for(let k=-6;k<=11;k++){ if(k===2) continue; if((-12-4*k)/(2-k)<4) n++ } return n
distractor_solve.12: let n=0; for(let k=-6;k<=11;k++){ if(-12-4*k < 4*(k-2)) n++ } return n

mechanism: k = 2 makes the coefficient vanish (no solution)
sign of k - 2 decides the inequality direction
count both branches in the range
quantity_asked: number of integers k with -6 ≤ k ≤ 11 for which the equation has a solution less than 4

setup.i: k multiplies a binomial in x on one side of a one-variable linear equation, so the x-coefficient k - 2 vanishes at one k
setup.ii: the solution is less than a stated number
setup.iii: number of integers k in a stated range

6.why: Keeping only the branch where k - 2 is negative omits k = 3 to 11; a student cannot see from the stem how the two branches compare in size.
